# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫳]

Thinking (not sent): I'm Deaf — I see the bomb, I never hear anything. Channel topology first: Mute can only reach me, and only by gesture (Mute cannot speak). Blind can reach Mute by voice, and me by gesture, but Blind can't hear gestures or see anything — so Blind can only ever receive my voice. That makes me the sole bridge between the manual and the hands: whatever Mute decides must pass through my mouth.

What I learned this round: Mute gestured me [🖐 ✌], [🖐], [☝] — with no shared code yet I can't trust any reading, though finger-counts (5-2, 5, 1) are the obvious guess. Blind sent [👋 🫳] — likely "hands here, awaiting orders." Nobody has bomb knowledge yet; Mute went first without seeing anything.

My move: dump the entire visible state in words — Mute needs it to read the manual, Blind needs the layout and colours to map under their fingers. Then fix a gesture key with Mute: finger-counts for numbers (matching what Mute already tried), plus yes/no and cut/press markers, so next round Mute can send me instructions as numbers and I relay them verbatim to Blind. I also warn Blind that my channel to them is voice-only, and that Mute's instructions arrive only through me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Full view of the bomb: display reads 9. Light is red. Strip painted green, then yellow, then yellow. Keypad: four keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 8, it expects 1 digit, nothing entered. Six wires left to right: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green. Your gestures 5-2, then 5, then 1 arrived, but I had no code yet. Ours starts now, shown as spoken: ☝ means 1, ✌ means 2, 🤟 means 3, 🖖 means 4, 🖐 means 5, 🤙 means 6. 👍 means yes, 👎 means no, 👊 means cut, ✊ means press or enter. Read the manual against what I gave you and answer me in gestures only, in this key. Anything meant for Blind, send in this key and I will speak it to Blind word for word. I cannot hear, so gestures are your only way to me.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I am the eyes. I cannot hear your voice, so signal me only with gestures. Layout to check by touch: six wires in a row, left to right: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green. Keypad of four keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 8, expecting one digit, nothing entered. Display reads 9, light is red, strip painted green then yellow then yellow. The manual-holder cannot reach you directly, so every instruction passes through my voice. Until one arrives, map everything by feel, but cut and press nothing.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "🖖", "🖐", "🤙", "👍", "👎", "👊", "✊"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Thinking (not sent): Decoding Mute's gestures against the key I established last round: [👊 🖐] = cut wire 5, [👊 🤟] = cut wire 3, [👊 🖖] = cut wire 4, [👎 ✊] = do not press/enter anything. That's a complete, confident sequence computed from my full turn-1 report — Mute is the only one who knows what the manual demands, and my job is faithful relay. But the board changed since Mute decided: display 9→3, light red→yellow. That drop pattern looks like a countdown nearing zero, and yellow-after-red reads as escalation — if I burn this round asking Mute to reconfirm, and it is a timer, we die waiting. If I cut and the rules were display/light-conditional, we die cutting. Mute has read the manual and knows what the display and light actually mean; they chose to send the cuts immediately rather than hold, which is their informed judgment on urgency. I follow it: Blind executes all three cuts now, in order, no keypad. Simultaneously I give Mute the updated readings so they can revise anything before remaining wires 1, 2, 6 are ever touched, and ask what the display and light mean per the manual so I can judge better next time. Blind also needs to know their report channels: their voice reaches Mute, not me — only gestures reach me.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Urgent instruction relayed from the manual-holder. Cut three wires, in this exact order, one at a time: first wire 5, second from the right end, the purple one; then wire 3, the middle-left of the six, the blue one; then wire 4, the middle-right, the red one. Do not press or enter anything on the keypad under any circumstances. For your fingers, left to right the six wires are: yellow, white, blue, red, purple, green; leftmost is 1. The display has dropped from 9 to 3 and the light turned yellow, which may mean time is short, so begin at once. When the three cuts are done, gesture me a thumbs up. Then speak aloud everything you felt during the cuts — the manual-holder can hear your voice, I cannot.")
speak(to="mute", text="Executing your sequence now through Blind: cut 5, then cut 3, then cut 4, nothing pressed — that is how I read your four messages; if I misread, correct me next round. Two updates since you decided: the display now reads 3, and the light has turned from red to yellow. If your rules depend on the display number or the light colour, gesture me a revised sequence immediately and I will relay it before any of the remaining wires 1 yellow, 2 white, 6 green are touched. Blind will report what they felt aloud, which you will hear directly. For next round, tell me: what does the manual say the display and the light mean, and what comes after the third cut — anything about the keypad 1, 5, 2, 8, or the strip green-yellow-yellow.")
```
